utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when those prisoners were brought in April?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: In the middle of that month.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: That was at the time, again, when the conflict escalated in the area?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I take it that it was as a result of the escalation in conflict that you could not come for work for five to six days thereafter?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I also take it that it was when you came to work thereafter that you saw that batch of Muslim civilians, Bosniaks, who had been brought to the Kaonik prison facility?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I did not have the opportunity to see them. I heard about it and I saw a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know who prepared that list?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: The supervisor, the supervisor of the security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said you did not see them, but you only heard about them?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Who told you that the Bosniaks had been brought during that period to the Kaonik prison facility?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Who told me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I saw a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said that you also saw and that you also heard about them. You said that you heard about them and that you also saw a list of prisoners who had been brought in the month of April of 1993.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: After arriving, well, I would -- it is normal to ask people what is new, did something new happen, and even that's my practice today. Whenever I arrive, I say, "Are there any new prisoners," so that I know how to distribute my workload, because there was not enough electricity and I had to type fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Aleksovski whether the prisoners had been brought in your absence?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: After arrival, I was immediately told that I would be very busy, that there is quite enough work for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Who told you that you would be very busy and that immediately they would have a lot of work for you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: In your discussion, did you mention the new batch of prisoners with Mr. Aleksovski at any point in time when you reported back to work?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Well, I did not have enough time because I didn't come there every day because I came there only once in five days or every second day. I didn't have enough time to talk. You had to enter all the data into the computer, because there were electricity cuts and there was electricity for only an hour or two or half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you have time to talk to him during periods when there were electricity cuts when you did not have to work on the computer?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I take it that it is during that time that you spoke to the prison warden and to the others within the prison facility?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Mrs. Vujica, do you remember any visits to the camp by members of international organisations?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you tell this court which international organisation visited the camp during this period?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: The Red Cross and sometimes the mission from the monitor would also arrive and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: When you say "monitor," you talk of the European Monitoring Commission, I presume?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, we called them monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember the members of the Monitoring Commission visiting the camp on the 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: If I show you a document, maybe I may be able to assist you with your memory, if I show you the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm showing this document to the witness, a document which has already been tendered into evidence, Your Honours, as P7. May P7 be placed on the ELMO, Your Honours, Prosecution Exhibit 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Mrs. Vujica, do you see this document that's on the ELMO now?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I take it that's a list that was prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: The document is dated the 10th of May, 1993. If we look at the top of the document, the top portion of the document, there's a date which is given as the 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Below that, it says, "List of prisoners of war." Isn't that what it says below that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes. I guess I made that list at the request of the person in charge who told me to make that list, and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Precisely, I mean, that was your function, when you were given instructions, to get outside instructions. Can you kindly look at that list and tell me whether there is a name of Rusmir Pasic which appears on that list that is on the ELMO before you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: There is another page to the document. I suggest that the witness be shown the second page as well, Your Honour. There's a second page to that.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I don't require it anymore, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, I take it that it is your testimony this morning that the Muslim prisoners who were detained in the Kaonik facility were well treated and well taken care of?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I think they were taken care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: In your estimation, were any of those prisoners badly treated by the guards or by members of the HVO or the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Is it that you don't know or is it your evidence that they were not badly treated?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think they were badly treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: It is also your evidence, I take it, that if they were badly treated, such prisoners (sic) would have been reported to the authorities concerned?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I think I have to repeat that question because I have used the word "prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I take it that if such prisoners are badly treated, whoever treated the prisoners badly, whether it be the guards or the soldiers, they would have been reported to the authorities concerned?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Well, to my mind, a prisoner or a civilian, they're all, to me, the same. They are all prisoners there and convicts too, because I'm there, I'm in a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And if any one of them, whether it be detainees, convicts, prisoners, civilians, any one of them, all those who are under disciplinary sanctions, if any one of them were badly treated by the soldiers or by the guards or by any of the shift commanders, I take it that it was routine duty to report them for such bad treatment to the authorities concerned?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: So I take it that because the prisoners were not badly treated by the guards or by the shift commanders, no such reports were made by the warden to the relevant authorities?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: We did report. If there were any excesses committed by the military policemen or soldiers, the warden would notify the district military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes, that is, if there were excesses committed, the district military court would be notified?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I take it that as it is your evidence that there were no such excesses, therefore, there were no such reports of maltreatment to the district military court or to any other relevant authority?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I wasn't there. I wasn't there. I had my working hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: But if such reports were made, I take it that you would have prepared such reports for the prison warden because it was part of your duty?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Wasn't it part of your duty to type all official letters and reports that went out of the prison under the hand of the prison warden?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: It was. So if such reports were to be made of excesses -- I hope you understand my question, if such excesses had taken place and reports were to be made, they would have been made by you to be forwarded under the hand of Mr. Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, dictated by Mr. Aleksovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Dictated by Mr. Aleksovski, thank you. So the fact remains that you did not prepare such reports to be sent to the relevant authorities?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Lordship, I must object to the manner in which my learned friend for the Prosecution is asking his questions. My learned friend asks his question assuming that a witness has done or has not done something. However, the Defence in adducing this evidence has already included a report which the witness present here had typed, so that is what she did. And the Prosecution now asks, "Since you didn't write the reports, it means that there were no excesses." So the Prosecution attributes to the witness the things that the witness never said, the witness said the contrary, and it's this that we object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, first, what do you say to the objection of Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I understand as elicited from the witness that she prepared reports when there were reports to be prepared. That is all. That is all and I have nothing more to elicit from this witness as regards the reports. It was her duty to prepare the reports. That was her evidence in chief in answer to my learned friend. I have elicited from her in cross-examination that it was indeed her duty and that there was no dereliction of duty whatsoever. I'm not suggesting that at all to the witness. I'm not in any way saying that this witness did not -- that there was any dereliction of duty on her part. She, in fact, did carry out here duties diligently. And whenever reports had to be prepared, she did prepare the reports. That is all the purpose of my cross-examination, Your Honours. I'm, in fact, moving on to the other document that the Defence produced to this witness, and I was about to ask -- the next question was to go on to that particular document that my learned friend just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But be that as it may, you may ask a direct question of the witness, whether she did or did not type the reports, dictated or drafted or drawn up by Mr. Aleksovski regarding excesses committed in the prison. You can ask it directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Your Honours, may the usher please give the witness document D25? Could it be placed on the ELMO, Mr. Usher? You can leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said this morning that this document, D25, which is on the ELMO, was typed by you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And that has on the top left-hand corner of that document, I believe it is the letterhead, the official letterhead which says that it is -- of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Although the date is illegible, it is a document prepared sometime in March of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And I find on the top right-hand corner of the document, there's some portion which has been either blocked out or there is an area which appears as if it has been blocked out. Yes, there.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And this is a report addressed -- it is a report under the hand of Mr. Aleksovski as the military prison commander?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: This blackened thing, it is the copying machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And it is a report under the hand -- I'm not attributing it to anything. I was just want to go place it on record that there was a black portion which is on the top right-hand corner of the document. I was not attributing any other discrepancy to that. Now, this is under the hand of Mr. Zlatko Aleksovski, the military prison commander?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said in your evidence that it is addressed to the president, but do you know to whom has it been addressed? Is it clear to you from the document?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: It is clear to you. And to whom has it been addressed?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: President of the military court in Travnik, Mr. Prcinlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: According to the contents of the report, a soldier by the name of Vlado Kristo --

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Kristo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you. Vlado Kristo had entered the military prison compound on the evening of the 26th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: That is what it says here. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Precisely. That's what the document says. I'm not saying that you were there. I'm just -- because you prepared that report, I'm trying to get out from you the contents of that document, and that's all. I'm not for the moment saying that you were present at the time when this incident took place. According to that report, Vlado Kristo had expressed his wish to see and allegedly identify a man named Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And since this Vlado Kristo, the soldier, had come out at official hours and, I believe, had not been in a fit condition to be admitted to the facility of the prison, and had not been given permission to talk with Krajisnik, that is, the detainee, the guards had refused his request to enter the prison facility?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Very well. And he had, however, threatened and insulted the military police personnel and got into his car and drove away?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I don't know. I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And the report says that. That's what I mean. The third paragraph of the report says that his attempt was thwarted by the guards, and he got in his car and started to threaten and insult the military police personnel?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: So on that occasion, the military police personnel, when there were such attempts, had thwarted attempts by soldiers to get access to the prison facility without proper permission?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it was their duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you, Ma'am. Ms. Registrar, may I have document 26, D26, Your Honours? I hope that it is clear to you on the screen, Witness? Is the document legible to you? Can you read the document?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Now, that is a document dated the 25th of March, 1993, and I take it that this was also prepared by you on the instructions of the prison warden?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And this also is a document under the hand of the prison warden, Mr. Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And it is also on the letterhead of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Below that are the words "Department of Justice and General Administration, Mostar, District Military Prison Kaonik, Busovaca."

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And in that, the prison commander has informed that the two cars are -- that is, a Fiat car and the Lada are no longer in working order?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Now, the Department of Justice and General Administration, that was one of the departments of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, of the government of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, ministry of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes. As much as the Department of Defence and the Department of the Interior and the several other departments that there were?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And these were all the departments that were established on the decree of the president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not need that document any longer, Your Honours. Your Honours, may I have a minute. Your Honours, I'm also tendering through this witness a document dated the 16th of May, 1993, a document handed over to me by my learned friend and that I'd use in the course of my case, Your Honours. There are sufficient copies for Your Honours and for the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, do you know this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, your Lordship, it is a document which I gave to my learned friend thinking to use it as evidence, but then I did not need it, so I didn't. But at any rate, it is a document which the Defence disclosed to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And you have no objections to the contrary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, we have no objections. This document is the one that we indicated to -- that we showed to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document of the Prosecution 135.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, the document before you, it's indicated the 16th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And it is a document of the Nikola Subic Zrinski Brigade of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And there's an order to send two prison guards and two detainees from the military-manned prison to the Prong (phoen) region as reinforcements on the defence line?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And copies of the document have been sent to the military prison commander, and I take it that that is Mr. Zlatko Aleksovski, and to your files?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: This has been made, this order has been made by Mr. Dusko Grubesic, the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Now, do you remember this order being sent to you or seeing this document in the office of Mr. Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you or did Mr. Aleksovski, in consequence of this document, send two detainees and prison guards to the Prong region, I take it, that is sent two detainees and prison guards?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know whether the names of these prisoners were entered on your registers before they were sent?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of those two prisoners or you do not?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, may I seize upon this break. Mrs. Blazenka, do you remember the name of the guard?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: All police officials were largely deployed along the frontline. Specifically during that time, there was a time when they were all sent to the frontline, and these two here, they are detainees who were there on the basis of the ruling of the district military court in Travnik. That is why they were posted there, except that they were bound to come to a district military prison to sleep and to report there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But don't you remember the names of the prisoners who were sent? I asked you if you could remember the names of the guards. There were two prisoners and two guards, and you told us that you could not remember the names of the prisoners. And I'm asking you, do you remember the names of the guards?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No, I do not remember who those guards were up there, because subsequently they all went to the line so that they organised shifts and replenished them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, I see. Thank you very much. Mr. Meddegoda, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your evidence was awhile ago that these were two detainees who were in the military prison on the orders of the district military court in Travnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And they were sent on this request, Mr. Aleksovski was the prison commander who authorised that they be sent as requested?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, in consultation with the president of the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions in cross-examination. Your Honours, I want to tender that document, Your Honours, into evidence as Exhibit P135.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, do you have any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence has just a few more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to bring to the witness the document which is entered into the register, under the marking P7, which she commented awhile ago in the cross-examination by the Prosecution. Could you put it, please, on the machine? So Mrs. Vujica, this is a document which you had the opportunity to see a few moments ago when my learned friend the Prosecutor had showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that this document was at the request of your European monitors, that was handed to the European monitors at their request?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us by looking at this document, what is it that you wrote there and what is there that you had not written? For instance, the title of that document up there, was it written by you, the list of Muslim war prisoners at Kaonik prison, did you write that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mrs. Vujica, also write, by hand, the comments in the right-hand of the document?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can we then say that it was additionally added to the document which you had originally written?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Vujica, you said that this document was written at the request of a European monitor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether it was a foreign or a national of your country?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I suppose that he was a foreigner because he had a translator with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is that then correct that you wrote what the translator or the interpreter told you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Vujica, did that interpreter tell you how to write the title of this document before the list?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the title, the list of war prisoners, was added when the European monitor asked you or actually his interpreter?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Correct, he or she, I can't remember, told me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you please turn to the second page of this document? Tell us, Mrs. Vujica, whether the added comments that are written by hand and not typed, are these -- was it also written by somebody else and not by you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, somebody else wrote those comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Vujica, we see that the document is signed by the warden of the district military prison, Zlatko Aleksovski, but there is no signature?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: There is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Because he was probably not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you have handed over this document at the request of European monitors in the absence of Mr. Zlatko Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence has no further questions for this witness. Mrs. Vujica, just one more question relating to the security situation. I will remind you, because you said in your statement that the situation, as far as the security was concerned, was not good, that there was shooting, that shells hit Kaonik itself, and that you couldn't go to work because it was dangerous; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You also said that you had to stay home with your own child to protect him to the best of your abilities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You also said, Mrs. Vujica, that you suppose that the Muslim civilians who were brought to Kaonik were brought there in addition to other things because of their own security?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I heard also that some of them came of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mrs. Vujica, if these Muslim civilian men were brought there for their own security, what happened to their children and their women?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: On the 25th of January, 1993, it was a Sunday when it all happened, and before that in Busovaca, it was market day, and everybody wondered why so many people would go into the direction of Kacuni with their livestock and children. We did not know why, but only tomorrow, a day later, we realised why did they go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Does it mean, Mrs. Vujica, that Muslim women and children, before the conflict, left Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So the houses of the Muslims who were brought to Kaonik, their women and children were not there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Vujica. The Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, there are some new elements, I do not know whether you wish to clarify some points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I have no matters to be clarified from those answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: You told us that in early February 1993, a group of prisoners was released. The Red Cross documents in which the recipients are the prisoners are dated on 29th April and 12th May. The other one is not dated. Are we talking about the same prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: The 25th of April, it must have been the group from another conflict, that was brought after another conflict, because the first group was released on the 8th of February, 1993, and the second group was released sometime in the middle of March -- of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mrs. Vujica, I should also like to ask you a few questions, if I may, perhaps to try to sum up your testimony. You told us that the district court in Travnik had supervisory authority over the prison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You also said that there were several categories of prisoners, that is, different categories of individuals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Could you please explain who were the prisoners or who were those or what were the individuals who were under the supervision of the Travnik court?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: These were the persons who were guilty of some criminal offences like robberies or -- and who were sentenced by the district court in Travnik and who were detained there on his orders, and they were detained in our district military prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: The witness said that the second group was released on May, and the transcript says on March.

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: The second group, depending on the situation, the security situation in that area, that is how the groups were released, depending on what the situation was, the Muslim civilians, so that the Red Cross at that time could not release all of them, so they had to be released in groups of five or ten people. I can't remember exactly how many of them were in those groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Does this answer satisfy you? All right. I shall continue then. You also said that the prison -- no, excuse me. Before I complete my question, if I have understood you properly, you said that the individuals, the prisoners who were under the supervision of the Travnik court were only individuals who had committed some disciplinary offences?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Crimes. Civil crimes or military crimes?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Then those civilians who were also Muslims, were they also supervised by the court in Travnik or not?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And they were under the supervision of whom?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Well, they were in charge of the Red Cross, the Red Cross took care of them. The warden also took care that they should have enough food, that somebody should not maltreat them or beat them, and they were under the control of the warden of the district military prison, because the role of the security guards and the whole -- the other personnel of the district prison was to protect those people as well as the detainees and people who were there for some disciplinary offences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, but the Red Cross did not bring those persons there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct. They were not brought there by the Red Cross, but the army brought them there, and they too took care of them in some way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So if I've understood you, what you said, there were some individuals, some prisoners who were under the supervision of the military court in Travnik, but was there another instance, some, perhaps, NGO which would be supervising individuals who were at Kaonik or wasn't there; do you know?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And another matter, Mrs. Blazenka. You said that the prison was a structure, a building. I've understood you to say that the prison was a civilian building? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, a civilian structure within the barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So it was a civilian building which was within the barracks, so military?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Another matter, you also told us that Mr. Aleksovski was assigned there by the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes. I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But then, is it true or not that this structure, this building was guarded by the military police, that is, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, could you then tell us how did it all function? There was a civilian structure integrated in a military compound -- military building. The prison warden was assigned there by the Ministry of Justice. The guards were, I suppose, posted by the Ministry of Defence, that is, HVO. So how did it all function together? What were the functions, the responsibilities of the warden, apart from assigning the guards on duty? Let me add something else. You said also that it was -- that the army was responsible for the supplies. What then did Mr. Aleksovski do there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksovski, well, his first role, and I suppose that it was the organisational structure of the military prison. He had to take care that the prison should function, and he made the house rules, which I typed, the house rules for the guards, for instance. And the same rules are applied today with some slight amendments. He also organised the bookkeeping, the records, and everything that is related to the running of a prison. It was all done at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But who was the superior? Who regulated the life in the prison? Was it Mr. Aleksovski or the HVO? Because --

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So it was Mr. Aleksovski who commanded, who truly commanded the prison?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, he was the warden, and the security, the prison was secured by military policemen who guarded the prisoners of all categories at his orders. And we reported disciplinary -- as far as discipline was concerned, to the military police, but we worked at the orders of Mr. Aleksovski, so there were no problems. And the military policemen fit in there quite nicely, and there were no problems between them and Mr. Aleksovski who was a civilian. And another remark, because the district prison in Busovaca is still part of the Kaonik barracks, and it is still -- the army is there, and we are a civilian prison, and the international police is inspecting us all the time and there is no problem with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, the rules that you spoke about, which were compounded by Mr. Aleksovski, were already in force when the Muslim civilians came?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I think, at least, because I met Mr. Aleksovski only after arriving, just as I arrived. It was ten days after the civilians were brought there. We had -- I think that the rules were made after, because there was some draft which I was supposed to type, and later, because he knew the rules in penitentiaries, so that is what he was doing. He had one copy from the house rules from the penitentiary in Tuzla and the district prison in Tuzla, and I still have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. Mrs. Blazenka, could one say at the end that Mr. Aleksovski ran the prison, bearing in mind that there were there the former barracks, and that one needed to adjust the installations for the new uses and organise the life and organise the functioning of the whole prison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Well, he could not control all the facilities, because all the facilities were not part of the prison. There was just one facility in the prison itself. And as for the hangar that is mentioned here, the hangar is now used as a warehouse. So it was a temporary facility because there was no -- there were not enough satisfactory conditions to accommodate all the civilians. Because the district prison of Busovaca had only 16 cells at the time, they were 4 by 4 roughly, so you can imagine how many people could be accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: And another matter, and that will be my last question. You said that the building was so solid, that it was built so well, so solidly, that it could resist all the damage from shelling?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But that is your opinion?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes, luckily not a single shell hit the facility, and if any shell had hit it, there must have been damage. They were just lucky.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, but according to you, perhaps that building was also solid -- built solidly in order to prevent the escape of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So it was solidly built for two reasons, for the security of the people who were there and also to prevent the prisoners, the detainees from fleeing?

utterances.speaker: BLAZENKA VUJICA
utterances.text: That building was not built for prisoners, because the original use was not as a district prison. This is what we inherited from the former JNA. I don't know when it was even built. I might not even be born at the time. I know that the walls are quite thick and quite solid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. Mrs. Blazenka, I think that the Chamber has no further questions to ask you. You have, therefore, completed your testimony here before the International Tribunal. Thank you very much for coming, and we wish you a pleasant journey home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, too. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, what shall we do now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence has also envisaged eight witnesses for this week, but because of objective reasons, we could not bring one witness, and we now have seven witnesses. Thanks to the efficient work, if I may say so, with the help of Your Honours and the Prosecution, the Defence has completed with its witnesses and we do not plan to bring any other witness this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If I may then, I need to consult my colleagues on a matter. All right. We shall now proceed to a closed session, because I think we should have something of a status conference to solve various matters, and will the technicians, please, take the necessary measures so that we can go into a closed session? Is it all right? Thank you very much.
